title: Bridging Design to Code: Exporting Multilingual SVG & Lottie Assets with Intact Arabic Shaping
excerpt: A senior frontend architect's guide to exporting arabic svg illustrator to web assets, fixing lottie animation arabic text broken workflows, and optimizing figma to react typography handoffs.
targetKeyword: export arabic svg illustrator to web, lottie animation arabic text broken fix, figma to react arabic typography workflow
content:
Exporting Arabic vector assets (SVG or JSON Lottie packages) from design tools like Illustrator, Figma, or After Effects frequently leads to disconnected letters, reversed word order, and corrupted glyph paths. When vector engines export unshaped text, the client browser renders raw, unmanaged Unicode code points from left to right instead of evaluating right-to-left cursive shaping.

Master native text shapers using our ultimate guide to fixing disconnected and reversed Arabic text, then follow this engineering pipeline to prepare clean production vector graphics.

Pro Tip: Always verify OpenType contextual shaping (initial, medial, final, and isolated forms) in your design tool BEFORE converting text to outlines. Outlining unshaped text bakes corrupt, detached glyphs directly into static vector paths.

Step-by-Step Pre-Export Pipeline for Arabic Vectors

To prevent client-side typography failures, implement this standardized asset preparation pipeline prior to bundling vector graphics into web applications:

  1. Enable Middle Eastern Text Composition: Set the active composition engine in your design software to World-Ready or Middle Eastern to resolve contextual ligatures correctly.
  2. Convert Live Text to Outlines: Flatten typography into vector compound paths to eliminate client-side font dependencies. For step-by-step software fixes, see our troubleshooting guide for Illustrator and Premiere Pro Arabic text.
  3. Unify Intersecting Path Geometry: Merge overlapping diacritics and complex script paths using pathfinder tools to eliminate SVG rendering artifacts.
  4. Isolate Lottie Animation Layers: Separate dynamic text layers from raster artwork and enable explicit right-to-left serialization settings in your motion export plugin.

Production Component Implementations

When embedding raw SVG markup inside React or Next.js components, use a dedicated wrapper container configured with directional styling attributes:

import React from 'react';

interface MultilingualAssetWrapperProps {
  svgContent: string;
  className?: string;
  ariaLabel: string;
}

export const MultilingualAssetWrapper: React.FC<MultilingualAssetWrapperProps> = ({
  svgContent,
  className = '',
  ariaLabel,
}) => {
  return (
    <div 
      dir="rtl"
      className={`flex items-center justify-center overflow-hidden ${className}`}
      role="img"
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: svgContent }}
    />
  );
};

For motion graphics rendering via Lottie, initialize the animation player with progressive loading options and explicit RTL layout flags:

import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import lottie from 'lottie-web';

export const ArabicLottiePlayer = ({ animationData }) => {
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!containerRef.current) return;

    const anim = lottie.loadAnimation({
      container: containerRef.current,
      renderer: 'svg',
      loop: true,
      autoplay: true,
      animationData,
      rendererSettings: {
        progressiveLoad: true,
        preserveAspectRatio: 'xMidYMid meet',
      },
    });

    return () => anim.destroy();
  }, [animationData]);

  return <div ref={containerRef} dir="rtl" className="w-full max-w-lg mx-auto" />;
};

Edge Case Troubleshooting Checklist

Production environments frequently surface edge cases even after proper pre-export processing. Use this checklist to quickly identify and isolate complex vector failures:

  • Distorted Path Coordinates After Outlining: Fonts with intricate diacritics often create overlapping vector paths. Use Illustrator's Pathfinder panel to merge intersecting paths into clean compound shapes before exporting.
  • Missing Glyphs in Lottie JSON Payloads: Web players struggle to parse complex cursive fonts from JSON files. Enable the "Convert Text to Shapes" option inside your extension export settings to store raw vector paths instead of font references.
  • Canvas Element Rendering Failures: Rendering dynamic text directly to HTML5 canvas viewports requires programmatic reshaping logic. Follow our comprehensive tutorial on Arabic reshaping in HTML5 canvas elements.
Pro Tip: Outlining text strips out semantic Unicode values, making vector text inaccessible to assistive technology. Always append explicit aria-label attributes or include screen-reader-only HTML text nodes alongside your vector assets.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Should I convert Arabic text to vector paths or rely on web fonts?

Convert text to outlines for static UI elements, logos, and iconography to guarantee visual consistency across devices. Use live DOM text nodes paired with OpenType web fonts and CSS RTL rules for user-generated or localized text strings, as detailed in our WordPress Arabic RTL fix masterclass.

2. How do I fix broken Arabic characters in Lottie animations?

Convert all text layers to shape layers inside your animation tool before exporting the JSON payload. This bakes the complex script geometry directly into the file schema and removes all runtime font rendering dependencies.

3. How do I ensure outlined SVG assets remain web accessible?

Outlined vector text loses its semantic meaning for assistive tools. Attach descriptive aria-label tags to parent container elements or add hidden semantic HTML text blocks adjacent to the visual SVG graphics.
